case: A terminated transaction backend rolls back table data but not an identity sequence increment
contract: The batch inserts a row using a PostgreSQL identity column, then blocks in SELECT pg_sleep(60) inside the same transaction.
A separate monitor identifies and terminates the active PostgreSQL backend.
The driver reports TransactionRollbackFailed at statement index 1, with the statement and rollback failures classified as disconnected.
A fresh query confirms the row was rolled back after backend termination.
A fresh query confirms last_value is 1 and is_called is true on the identity sequence, documenting PostgreSQL's non-transactional sequence side effect.

focused_test.command: rtk proxy cargo test --locked -p tablepro-driver-postgres --test integration a_batch_reports_rollback_failure_after_postgres_terminates_its_backend -- --ignored --exact --test-threads=1

format_and_diff.command: rtk cargo fmt --all -- --check; rtk git diff --check

remaining: Re-run on the frozen B3+B4 candidate SHA and hosted CI.
This proves one PostgreSQL identity-sequence side effect only; it does not cover all trigger, extension, or external effects.
